claims.claim_text: FCEL recognized $66.0 million of product revenue in FY2025 under its LTSA with Gyeonggi Green Energy (GGE) for replacement of 22 fuel cell modules at the 58.8 MW Hwaseong-si South Korea plant. GGE represents the overwhelming majority of FCEL's $69.1M product revenue and is a binding, ongoing commercial counterparty.
claims.subject: FuelCell Energy
claims.object_value: Gyeonggi Green Energy (Korea Southern Power affiliated) under LTSA; ~$66M of FY25 product revenue
claims.source_quote: increase in product revenues during the year ended October 31, 2025 was primarily driven by $66.0 million of revenue recognized under the Company's LTSA with GGE for the replacement of 22 fuel cell modules for GGE's 58.8 MW fuel cell power plant platform in Hwasong-si, South Korea

claims.claim_text: FCEL closed a $25.0M EXIM-backed project debt financing on Nov 26, 2025 at 5.29% to support the GGE LTSA; total minimum cash balance covenant reduced from $100M to $55M concurrently.
claims.subject: FuelCell Energy
claims.object_value: Export-Import Bank of the United States; $25.0M gross / $23.1M net; 5.29% fixed; 7-year amortization
claims.source_quote: On November 26, 2025, the Company closed on its second project debt financing transaction (the 2025 EXIM Financing) with the Export-Import Bank of the United States... resulting in gross proceeds of approximately $25.0 million. Interest accrues at a fixed interest rate of 5.29%

claims.claim_text: FCEL pitches its 1.25 MW carbonate modules as the on-site behind-the-meter solution for hyperscaler data centers; markets modularity for 'hundreds of megawatts' of demand and contrasts vs. 5-7 year utility interconnection timelines. No specific hyperscaler counterparty (AMZN, MSFT, META, GOOGL) is named in the 10-K as a contracted customer.
claims.subject: FuelCell Energy
claims.object_value: hyperscaler / AI data-center power; modular 1.25 MW power blocks; 33 MW/acre density
claims.source_quote: Our modular products are 1.25 MW power blocks (or modules) that can be scaled to meet hundreds of megawatts of demand... can help to maximize output even in space-constrained environments... carbonate fuel cell platform delivers baseload power to critical loads

claims.claim_text: FCEL operates a Toyota tri-generation hydrogen+power project (Port of Long Beach) under a 20-year hydrogen production and PPA, with three years of fixed-price natural gas through May 2026; fuel exposure flagged as material risk. Listed as one of four 'projects with fuel sourcing risk'.
claims.subject: FuelCell Energy
claims.object_value: Toyota Motor North America; PPA + H2 offtake; fixed-price fuel through May 2026
claims.source_quote: the initial three years of the twenty year hydrogen production and power purchase agreement for our Toyota project (through May of 2026)... four projects with fuel sourcing risk, which are the Toyota project

claims.claim_text: FCEL effected a 1-for-30 reverse stock split on Nov 8, 2024 (611.3M to 20.4M shares), then sold 25.6M additional shares for $190.4M gross under the ATM in FY2025 (with another ~16.4M in Q4 alone). Cumulative share count expansion in 12 months effectively reversed the split. This is a textbook distress / dilution pattern.
claims.subject: FuelCell Energy
claims.object_value: 1-for-30 reverse split Nov 2024; ~25.6M ATM shares FY25; ~$190M gross ATM proceeds; chronic losses
claims.source_quote: On November 8, 2024, we effected a 1-for-30 reverse stock split, reducing the number of our common shares outstanding on that date from 611,278,662 shares to approximately 20,375,932 shares... approximately 25.6 million shares of the Company's common stock were sold under the Sales Agreement at an average sale price of $7.44 per share, resulting in gross proceeds of approximately $190.4 million

claims.source_quote: we manufacture and sell our proprietary molten carbonate fuel cell systems... claims.claim_text: Product backlog declined from $111.3M (Oct 2024) to $66.2M (Oct 2025), a 41% decrease, despite revenue growth driven by GGE module consumption. Service backlog also down ($174.2M -> $162.4M). Implies replenishment pipeline shrinking even as headline revenue grows.
claims.subject: FuelCell Energy
claims.object_value: product backlog $66.2M (-41% YoY); service backlog $162.4M (-7% YoY)
claims.source_quote: As of October 31, 2025 and 2024, there was $66.2 million and $111.3 million, respectively, of product backlog... service agreements backlog totaled $162.4 million compared to $174.2 million as of October 31, 2024
